category_title: Struggling readers who use direct repetition of previous text to avoid new reading
scenario_title: Shared reading turn-taking avoidance via repetition
minimal_context: The student and interventionist are taking turns reading 'Miss Nelson is missing!' together.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's continue reading 'Miss Nelson is missing!'. I will read this sentence: 'The class was rude.' Now it is your turn.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: I just read that part. Please look at the next line and read it.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Accepts the speaking turn but does not attempt the unread text) Was rude.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: (Points to the next passage of text) Go ahead and read this next one.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: You 's gonna read the next one. I read this one.

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: Let's continue reading 'Miss Nelson is missing!'. I will read this sentence: 'The class was rude.' Now it is your turn.

STUDENT: Was rude or that one.

TUTOR: I just read that part. Please look at the next line and read it.

STUDENT: (Accepts the speaking turn but does not attempt the unread text) Was rude.

TUTOR: (Points to the next passage of text) Go ahead and read this next one.

STUDENT: You 's gonna read the next one. I read this one.
